what: Sage fp8++ rotated as Sol's dense fallback against kitchen int8 (the shipped chain), wall time only, on the t2v finish. Owner-approved 2026-10-01 (review1001), reopening the lane docs/state/next_steps.md parked under the Sol node redesign.
why: Kitchen int8 is the more accurate dense kernel on all 12 dense-tail cells (bench/results/2026-09-27_sol_redesign_test2.md, 'The dense tail'), so a sage case rests on speed, or on the early dense steps that no capture has graded; bench/sage_floor_capture_arms.json grades those. A rendered clip cannot A/B a numerical change, so these renders are timed, not judged.
build: the sage arm is the generator's own sage chain (h3_config.DENSE_CHAINS['sage']): build_workflows.py --chain sage --out internal/chain_sage, validated against the live server. Its only difference from the shipped graph is MiniMaxH3SageAttention in place of ModelAttentionBackend.
order: alternating kitchen, sage, kitchen, sage after one warmup, so drift is shared; same prompt throughout, so the text encode is paid once.
